First-time divers

Curious about your first breath underwater?

You don't need to know every piece of equipment to begin asking questions. Tell W Divers you're new to scuba, and ask about introductory options for your dates.

An introduction is different from a certification.

An introductory experience offers a supervised first taste of scuba. A certification course follows a structured training pathway. Ask which format is available and appropriate for you.

Before you choose an experience.

Confirm eligibility, minimum age, swimming or water-comfort expectations, required screening, supervision, duration and the location of the activity. Mention concerns directly to the team; an inquiry form is not a medical clearance.

No need to pretend you're confident already.

It's fine to have questions about breathing underwater, equipment or being in the sea. Describe what you're comfortable with so the conversation starts in the right place.

Questions worth asking

For people who have never tried scuba, or tried it long ago.

  • Eligibility and minimum age
  • Swimming or water-comfort expectations
  • Required screening
  • Supervision
  • Duration and location
